cues.zh: 从前，
cues.en: Once upon a time,

cues.en: which means about .05 percent is named Lester.

cues.en: Now, Lesters in Lesterland have this extraordinary power.

cues.zh: 一场叫大选。
cues.en: One is called the general election.

cues.en: The other is called the Lester election.

cues.en: And in the general election, it's the citizens who get to vote,

cues.zh: 但在莱斯特选举中，是莱斯特们来投票。
cues.en: but in the Lester election, it's the Lesters who get to vote.

cues.zh: 这里有个玄机。
cues.en: And here's the trick.

cues.zh: 要想参加大选，
cues.en: In order to run in the general election,

cues.zh: 你必须在
cues.en: you must do extremely well

cues.en: in the Lester election.

cues.zh: 你不一定要赢，但必须表现得极其出色。
cues.en: You don't necessarily have to win, but you must do extremely well.

cues.zh: 那么，关于 Lesterland 的民主，我们能说些什么？
cues.en: Now, what can we say about democracy in Lesterland?

cues.zh: 能说的是，第一，
cues.en: What we can say, number one,

cues.zh: 正如最高法院在 Citizens United 案中所说，
cues.en: as the Supreme Court said in Citizens United,

cues.zh: 人民对民选官员拥有最终的影响力，
cues.en: that people have the ultimate influence over elected officials,

cues.zh: 因为毕竟还有大选，
cues.en: because, after all, there is a general election,

cues.zh: 但前提是 Lesters 已经按自己的意愿
cues.en: but only after the Lesters have had their way

cues.zh: 筛选了那些想参加大选的候选人。
cues.en: with the candidates who wish to run in the general election.

cues.zh: 第二，显然，这种对 Lesters 的依赖
cues.en: And number two, obviously, this dependence upon the Lesters

cues.zh: 会催生一种微妙的、不露痕迹的、
cues.en: is going to produce a subtle, understated,

cues.zh: 可以说隐蔽的、
cues.en: we could say camouflaged, bending

cues.zh: 为了讨好 Lesters 的扭曲。
cues.en: to keep the Lesters happy.

cues.zh: 好，所以我们确实有民主，毫无疑问，
cues.en: Okay, so we have a democracy, no doubt,

cues.zh: 但它依赖于 Lesters，
cues.en: but it's dependent upon the Lesters

cues.en: and dependent upon the people.

cues.en: It has competing dependencies,

cues.en: we could say conflicting dependencies,

cues.en: depending upon who the Lesters are.

cues.en: Okay. That's Lesterland.

cues.en: Now there are three things I want you to see now that I've described Lesterland.

cues.en: Number one, the United States is Lesterland.

cues.en: The United States is Lesterland.

cues.en: The United States also looks like this, also has two elections,

cues.en: one we called the general election,

cues.en: the second we should call the money election.

cues.en: In the general election, it's the citizens who get to vote,

cues.en: if you're over 18, in some states if you have an ID.

cues.en: you must do extremely well in the money election.

cues.en: You don't necessarily have to win. There is Jerry Brown.

cues.en: But you must do extremely well.

cues.en: And here's the key: There are just as few relevant funders

cues.en: in USA-land as there are Lesters in Lesterland.

cues.en: Now you say, really?

cues.en: Really .05 percent?

cues.en: .26 percent of America

cues.en: .05 percent gave the maximum amount to any federal candidate,

cues.zh: 0.01%——也就是百分之一中的百分之一——
cues.en: .01 percent -- the one percent of the one percent --

cues.en: gave 10,000 dollars or more to federal candidates,

cues.zh: 而在本次选举周期中，我最喜欢的统计数字
cues.en: and in this election cycle, my favorite statistic
is .000042 percent

cues.en: gave 60 percent of the Super PAC money spent

cues.en: in the cycle we have just seen ending.

cues.en: So I'm just a lawyer, I look at this range of numbers,

cues.zh: 我就觉得，我可以公平地说
cues.en: and I say it's fair for me to say

cues.en: it's .05 percent who are our relevant funders in America.

cues.zh: 从这个意义上说，资助者就是我们的莱斯特。
cues.en: In this sense, the funders are our Lesters.

cues.en: Now, what can we say about this democracy in USA-land?

cues.en: Well, as the Supreme Court said in Citizens United,

cues.en: but only after the funders have had their way

cues.en: with the candidates who wish to run in that general election.

cues.en: And number two, obviously,

cues.en: this dependence upon the funders

cues.en: Candidates for Congress and members of Congress

cues.en: spend between 30 and 70 percent of their time

cues.en: raising money to get back to Congress

cues.en: or to get their party back into power,

cues.en: and the question we need to ask is, what does it do to them,

cues.en: these humans, as they spend their time

cues.en: behind the telephone, calling people they've never met,

cues.zh: 却是打给那百分之一里最微小的一撮人？
cues.en: but calling the tiniest slice of the one percent?

cues.zh: 任何人都会这样，在做的过程中，
cues.en: As anyone would, as they do this,

cues.en: they develop a sixth sense, a constant awareness

cues.en: about how what they do might affect their ability to raise money.

cues.en: They become, in the words of "The X-Files,"

cues.en: shape-shifters, as they constantly adjust their views

cues.en: but on issues 11 to 1,000.

cues.en: worse than Lesterland because you can imagine in Lesterland

cues.en: I don't mean any criminal act.

cues.en: The corruption I'm talking about is perfectly legal.

cues.en: and by a representative democracy, they meant a government,

cues.en: but it's different and conflicting from a dependence upon the people alone

cues.en: This is a corruption.

cues.en: It blocks the left on a whole range of issues that we on the left really care about.

cues.en: It blocks the right too, as it makes

cues.en: So the right wants smaller government.
